_about: Public-domain Jedidiah Morse (1761-1826), Congregational minister at Charlestown, founder of Andover Seminary's party and opponent of Harvard Unitarianism, for the Word Hoard: his sermons (1795-1810), The True Reasons on which the Election of a Hollis Professor was Opposed, the African Meeting-House discourse, and An Appeal to the Public. His geographies and gazetteers are left out as not theology. Texts are from Internet Archive scans. Added 2026-10-23 by lane A, round 96 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

morse-present-situation: The present situation of other nations of the world, contrasted with our own. : a sermon, delivered at Charlestown, in the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, February 19, 1795 ; being the day recommended by George Washington, president of the United States of America, for publick thanksgiving and prayer (Boston : [publisher not identified], 1795)
morse-grand-lodge: A sermon delivered before the Grand Lodge of free & accepted masons of the commonwealth of Massachusetts, at a public installation of the officers of the Corinthian Lodge, at Concord, ... June 25th, 1798. By Jedediah Morse, ...  1798 (catalogued 1798)
morse-thanksgiving-1798: A sermon, preached at Charlestown, November 29, 1798, on the anniversary thanksgiving in Massachusetts. With an appendix, ... by Jedidiah Morse, ...  1798 (catalogued 1798)
morse-faithful-servant: The character and reward of a good and faithful servant illustrated in a sermon, delivered at Charlestown, April 29, 1798, the Lord's-Day following the death and interment of the Honorable James Russell, ... By ...  1798 (catalogued 1798)
morse-present-dangers: A sermon, exhibiting the present dangers, and consequent duties of the citizens of the United States of America : Delivered at Charlestown, April 25, 1799. The day of the national fast (Charlestown [Mass.]: : Printed and sold by Samuel Etheridge, next door to Warren-Tavern., 1799)

morse-african-meeting-house: A discourse, delivered at the African Meeting-House, in Boston, July 14, 1808 : in grateful celebration of the abolition of the African slave-trade, by the governments of the U.S., Great Britain, and Denmark (Boston : Printed by Lincoln & Edmands, 1808)
morse-signs-of-times: Signs of the times. A sermon, preached before the Society for Propagating the Gospel among the Indians and Others in North America, at their anniversary, Nov. 1, 1810 (Charlestown [Mass.] Printed for the benefit of the Society, by S.T. Armstrong, 1810)
